newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - July 2.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - July 2.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

PARIS - France's new Health Minister, Bernard Kouchner, says he will introduce new requirements for health warnings on cigarette packets and will not tolerate alcohol brands using the World Cup football tournament as a shop window.

LONDON - British Consumer Affairs Minister Nigel Griffiths rules out introducing statutory regulation of the advertising industry in the foreseeable future, saying the existing self-regulatory system adequately protects consumers.
CHICAGO - Leo Burnett Worldwide forms a joint venture with Wirz Advertising of Vienna to service its international clients in Austria.
PARIS - Connect World, the multimedia unit of Havas Advertising, says it has been appointed by Peugeot Citroen to create and run its World Wide Web site on the Internet.

DUBAI - Advertising expenditure in six Gulf Arab states between January and May 1997 rose to $334 million from $293 million in the same period in 1996, the Pan Arab Research Centre says. Saudi Arabia is the biggest advertising market with 18 million citizens.

MINNEAPOLIS - International Dairy Queen Inc says it has selected Grey Advertising Inc as its new agency of record for the U.S. portion of its "Dairy Queen" account. Full details of the agreement have not been disclosed, but the company says the Dairy Queen chain's estimated media billing for 1998 will be $25 million.

TOKYO - Dentsu Inc, the world's largest advertising agency, says it is raising new capital, expanding its business and plans to make 1.5 trillion yen ($13.1 billion) in annual sales by the year 2000. Dentsu, which made 1.28 trillion yen in sales in the year ending March 1997, says it plans to raise new capital by issuing 300,000 new shares.
BRISBANE - Australian Provincial Newspapers Holdings Ltd is to form a dedictated street furniture division to run seat and bus shelter advertising.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

NEW YORK - Westinghouse Electric Corp denies newspaper reports that it is looking to sell its CBS media business to Microsoft Corp. And Microsoft, which has close ties to General Electric's NBC network, separately says it has no plans to buy CBS.

CAPE TOWN - Long dominated by English-speaking interests, South Africa's media is in flux and newspapers who cater for Afrikaans speakers may be the winners. The language is now one of the most widely spoken in the country and advertisers are flocking to support Afrikaans publications, say industry experts.

PARIS - Shares in French pay television group Canal Plus rise on expectations that the group will get control of Italy's Telepiu. The Canal Plus board is set to meet and agree a deal with German media groups Bertelsmann and Kirch under which the French group will swap its stake in German pay television group Premiere for Kirch's stake in Telepiu and a cash payment, industry experts say.
MUNICH - German television group Pro Sieben AG, in the middle of an initial public offering, says its market share of German viewers for its two domestic networks rose slightly in June.

LONDON - Britain's Independent Television Commission watchdog urges the government to phase out the Channel 4 funding formula by the end of next year. Designed as a system of income support for state-owned C4, the success of the channel has meant that the ITV commercial television companies have been receiving hefty annual payments from C4.
CHICAGO - Playboy Enterprises Inc. says it plans to publish a Scandinavian edition of Playboy magazine.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

VERS-CHEZ-LES-BLANC, Switzerland - The pressure is on at Nestle to develop smash-hit products to follow its original infant formula, the Maggi stock cube and Nescafe instant coffee. "I can assure you that Nescafe will not be our last blockbuster," a spokesman says.
CHICAGO - McDonald's Corp, which a month ago cancelled most of its nationwide Campaign 55 price promotion, saw a decline in June same-store sales of up to eight percent, analysts say.
SEATTLE - Sports footwear and apparel giant Nike Inc. says its fourth-quarter profits rose 17 percent, reflecting a slowdown in growth.
PARIS - Car sales in France fell 30.7 percent last month, the worst June performance since 1962, as price-cutting failed to entice anxious consumers, industry officials say.
STOCKHOLM - Swedish car maker Saab Automobile AB says its sales in the U.S. rose 15 percent to 3,761 vehicles in June compared to June 1996.
LONDON - British financial services and tobacco group B.A.T Industries Plc will soon announce plans for a full demerger to be completed by next year, the Guardian newspaper reports.
CONSUMER TRENDS:
WASHINGTON - Three out of every 10 U.S. households were headed by women in 1996, according to new data released by the Commerce Department's Census Bureau.

LONDON - British legislators file a motion in parliament to stop a trend towards giving pubs bizarre new names such as the Philanderer and Firkin, the Purple Turtle or the Rat and Parrot, which is enraging traditionalists.

LONDON - Micro Compact Car AG, manufacturers of the tiny Smart car, say it is a revolution in the making which will change urban motoring for ever. But detractors say consumers will find the car too small, too expensive and too ugly.

JAKARTA - Indonesia hopes the hero of a new movie -- a 16th-century Islamic cleric -- will prove a saviour to the country's neglected film industry, which is under siege as consumers rush to see slick foreign imports.

PALERMO, Sicily - The president of Sicily's anti-Mafia committee, Fabio Granata, lashes out at a German travel agency which wants to set up special tours of the island taking in grisly Mafia murder sites.
